js.lean: No bet-worthy edge on the side or total: the blended number (CHA +3.0, total 227.3) is within about half a point of the market (CHA -2.5, 227.5), so the slight Charlotte lean is not worth backing.

WAS gets to the line (FT rate 0.402) but CHA's defense allows only 0.276. CHA's offense turns it over often (TOV% 0.198), which cancels some of its offensive-rebounding edge (ORB% 0.324 vs WAS allowing 0.285).

risks: Three-game samples make every rating, shot-zone figure and prop average unstable, and one blowout (ATL 128-81) distorts the CHA numbers.

The total moves with Charlotte's pace, because WAS runs 105.7 and CHA 102.3. A 3-point-heavy shot mix adds variance to the total.
matchups: Trae Young (36.3 min, 11.3 ast) and the WAS guards against CHA's small backcourt of Schroder and Allen (from memory, roles may have changed after the 2026 offseason).
Kalkbrenner and Diabate at the rim against Anthony Davis and Sarr: WAS allows 35% of shots at the rim, so CHA's rim rate (29%) could rise.
verify: Naz Reid's final status. The prop model applies a +1 minute bump for 'Reid out' while the report lists him probable, so I reversed that bump with mult 0.96 on the affected CHA props.
